<thought>Based on the observed [M+H]⁺ peak at m/z 183.045 (neutral mass ≈ 182.038 Da) and the relatively intense M+2 peak (~32 % of the base), the isotopic pattern suggests the presence of one chlorine atom (which gives a characteristic M+2 ≈ 24 % intensity). Subtracting the chlorine mass (34.969 Da) leaves a remaining mass of ≈ 147.069 Da, which fits well with a formula containing nine carbons, seven hydrogens, and two oxygens. The calculated monoisotopic mass for C₉H₇O₂Cl is 182.013 Da, within experimental error, and the combined ¹³C and ³⁷Cl contributions explain the observed M+2 intensity. Therefore, the most plausible molecular formula is C₉H₇O₂Cl.</thought>
<final_answer>C9H7O2Cl</final_answer>
